{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive Summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are strong for us and require no redline: Vendor indemnification (§ 20), ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data (§ 14), limitation of liability including the mutual cap and Excluded Claims (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), governing law and venue (§ 28), no minimum commitment (§ 2.1), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), and Vendor insurance (§ 18).

The issues are concentrated in a small set of Customer-burdening provisions, three of which sit at our walk-away positions: full-term exclusivity/non-compete on Customer (§ 2.2), uncapped daily liquidated damages payable by Customer (§ 7.6), a wrong-direction most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), and unlimited unannounced Vendor audit with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1). Notably, §§ 2.1 and 12.3 already record that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment, so §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 conflict with the parties' stated bargain and should be corrected rather than merely narrowed.

We also flag one gap: there is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere in the Agreement, against a three-year committed term under § 8.1. Remaining items (auto-renewal notice window, Customer-side non-solicit, Deliverable warranty duration) are straightforward negotiated fixes.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 | Unqualified IP defence/indemnity to Customer, Affiliates and personnel; balanced procedure; carved out of the cap as an Excluded Claim under § 21.3. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 | Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables (present assignment); embedded Vendor Technology routed to the perpetual § 13.2 licence; no joint ownership. No redline. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000; all required carve-outs outside the cap under § 21.3. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate or successor; Vendor assignment consent-gated; no Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control (§ 24.4). No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 | Full-term sole and exclusive provider obligation with no category, time or performance-based exit — walk-away position; conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3. Delete. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 7.6 | USD 25,000/day for any dependency delay, with no materiality threshold, cure period or aggregate limit; 40 days alone would exhaust the § 21.1 cap. Delete and substitute excused performance plus equitable schedule adjustment. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 | Grant extends to Affiliates and contractors; § 13.2 perpetual paid-up licence; transferability and cure-gated suspension in § 13.3. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 | Same clause imposes a field-of-use restriction on what we may buy or build; contradicts § 12.3. Convert to a non-exclusive appointment with express confirmation of no restriction on Customer's business. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9.3 | Section 9 provides only breach, insolvency and Vendor security/SLA/legal/IP termination; no convenience right against the three-year term in § 8.1. Add § 9.4 (30 days, pro-rata refund via § 10.2, no reciprocal Vendor right). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced Vendor audits plus remote access to our systems — walk-away position; §§ 22.2–22.3 already comply. Rewrite § 22.1 for frequency, notice, scope and access limits. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 | New York law, CISG excluded, exclusive New York County state and federal courts; no arbitration; escalation does not delay urgent relief. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Wrong-direction, open-ended MFN binding Customer; contradicts § 12.3. Delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 | No minimum quantity or purchase commitment; § 7.1 bars minimum-use charges; § 12.3 confirms no volume commitment. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 18-month no-solicit/no-engage covering any Vendor employee during the term, no carve-outs; sits uneasily with § 12.3. Narrow to mutual, 12-month, solicitation-only, Services personnel, with advertising and inbound carve-outs. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 8.2 | 180-day non-renewal notice exceeds our 30-day preferred and 60-day fallback; § 8.3 uplift cap already compliant. Reduce to 30 days plus a Vendor 60-day reminder. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; 30-day machine-readable data return with no fee-dispute withholding; certified deletion only after confirmed return. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M for term plus one year; § 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability. No redline. |
| Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 | Deliverable conformance limited to 90 days against our 12-month preferred position for software; Hosted Services already warranted for the term. Extend § 19.2 to twelve (12) months; fallback 90 days with § 19.4 remedies untouched. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following sit at our playbook walk-away positions and should be resolved before signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity / non-compete on Customer.** Full-term sole and exclusive provider obligation with no category limit, time limit or performance-based exit. It also conflicts with § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity or non-compete commitment). Preferred remedy is deletion; fallback is a defined category, 12 months, with automatic termination on SLA or delivery failure.
2. **§ 7.6 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, with no materiality threshold, cure period or aggregate cap. Because the § 21.1 cap is measured against 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, roughly 40 days of delay would exhaust it. Our playbook permits no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
3. **§ 7.2 — Wrong-direction MFN.** Open-ended obligation to give Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms offered to any other technology supplier, with no defined product, time limit or comparison carve-outs, and directly contrary to § 12.3. Deletion is the minimal edit.
4. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit of Customer.** Audits at any time without notice plus remote access to our systems. Our position permits no more than one audit per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-only with no access to Customer systems.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the verified proposals: delete § 2.2 (and confirm non-exclusivity with no restriction on Customer's business); delete § 7.2; delete § 7.6 and substitute excused Vendor performance with an equitable schedule adjustment; rewrite § 22.1 with the frequency, notice, scope and access limits.
2. **Add § 9.4** granting Customer a 30-day termination-for-convenience right without penalty, keyed to the prepaid-fee refund mechanics in § 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a term.
3. **Negotiate the secondary items:** reduce the § 8.2 non-renewal notice to 30 days with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal (fallback 60 days); narrow § 12.4 to a mutual, 12-month, solicitation-only restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express deletion of any no-hire; extend the § 19.2 Deliverable conformance period to twelve (12) months, with a 90-day fallback leaving the § 19.4 remedy intact.
4. **Leverage the internal inconsistencies.** Sections 2.1 and 12.3 already record that we made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We should present §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 as conforming edits to the parties' stated bargain rather than as new asks.
5. **Confirm no further movement is sought** on the compliant provisions (§§ 11, 13, 14, 18, 20, 21, 24, 28 and 2.1) so that reciprocal Vendor requests in those areas can be resisted.
6. **Escalate** if Vendor declines to move on any of the four walk-away items, and report back to the deal team before further drafting."}
